as_told.title: CIA Office of Global Access, JSOC and NEST in crash retrievals

plain: This story is about the Office of Global Access, said to be a unit of the CIA, the US spy agency, and reporting about it in the British newspaper the Daily Mail around 2023 and 2024. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that, according to that reporting, this office is the main part of a programme that recovers crashed craft of unknown origin all around the world. He links it to a man named Doug Wolf, saying the office did rapid-response retrievals in the early 2000s under him. An online researcher known as UAPGerb says a journalist named Christopher Sharp broke the story, and that the office was created in 2003 inside the CIA's Directorate of Science and Technology, its branch for technical work. Michels adds on a later episode that the office is rumoured to work closely with JSOC, the command for America's elite special forces, and with NEST, the Nuclear Emergency Support Teams. If true, it would mean the CIA runs a standing worldwide operation to collect crashed non-human craft.
